subject: Failure to initialise after specifying upper bound

messages.author: abab84dd2ba42997
messages.subject: Failure to initialise after specifying upper bound
parts:
Hi Stan users group,

I am working some more on a model that has previously revealed some memory issues (see this topic). 

I have encountered something a bit weird with a variant of the model (attached). You will see that the parameters "p" and "mu_p" are given upper bounds of 10. With the attached data, the model fails to initialise after 100 attempts. However, if you now remove the upper bounds on these parameters, the model initialises just fine. 

In the testing I have tried, specifying pretty much any upper bound on p gives this failure, whether or not the other parameters also have upper bounds. If p is left unbounded, it doesn't produce initial values larger than the upper bound I've given (note prior on p).

Any thoughts?

Tom

We were able to fix the memory issues that your other model touched. (Thanks for alerting us to that!)

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure to initialise after specifying upper bound
parts:
Hi Tom,

The issue has to do with initial values for constrained variables (and it touches on underflow). The manual covers both these things in full detail in:
* Chapter 20.2. "Initialization." See the section on "Random Initial Values."
* Chapter 49. "Transformations of Variables"

I'll try to add some concrete examples, but I would suggest re-reading those sections.


From Tom's model:

Without the upper bound:

We'll just take a look at one of the variables, mu_p. It was originally declared as
    real<lower=0> mu_p;
   
with a prior of:
    mu_p ~ lognormal(log(2.0), 1);  // or lognormal(0.7, 1)

The defaults of Stan will initialize the *unconstrained* variable uniformly from -2 to 2. This puts the constrained variable, the mu_p, on a range of 0.13=exp(-2) to 7.39=exp(2), with the unconstrained value of 0 being mapped to a constrained value of 1=exp(0).

[In theory, since lognormal has support over where the parameter is constrained, this should work out just fine. In practice, due to restrictions on floating point arithmetic, some of these calculations will underflow and it isn't fine. At some value of mu_p way outside the prior mass, the calculation will underflow and the evaluation of lognormal_log(mu_p, 0.7, 1) will return -Inf. It's hard to add -Inf to other numbers without the result being -Inf or NaN.]

So, without the upper constraint on mu_p, there's a chance this will get initialized properly if the unconstrained value is sampled from -2 to 0 (I'm eyeballing it). In the model, p is also given the same constraint and there are 25k of those.

In some sense, it's amazing that the model initializes to something that it can calculate by randomly choosing starting values from -2 to 2 on the unconstrained scale.

With the upper bound

Let's change the parameter and see where the initialization takes us.
   real<lower=0,upper=10> mu_p;

Going into the manual, Chapter 49.4, "Lower and Upper Bounded Scalar," we see that the transformation is:
   X = a + (b - a) * logit^-1(Y),
where a is the lower bound, b is the upper bound, and Y is the unconstrained value.

So (-2, 0, 2) on the unconstrained scale corresponds to (1.2, 5, 8.9) on the constrained scale. That looks high.

This variable alone won't cause a problem, but having 25k other variables and other calculations pushes the calculation to -Inf.


Simple Example: uniform

Here's a simple example. The difference with uniform is that there isn't support everywhere, so it's easier to make it fail. This model works fine.

parameters {
  real theta;
}
model {
  theta ~ uniform(-1, 1);
}

Let's change theta to have a lower bound of 0 and an upper bound of 10.
  real<lower=0,upper=10> theta;

Stan can't find an appropriate starting value.



Possible Fixes

Here are a couple of possible fixes.
  1. Provide initial values. Help your model out a bit. Give it starting values that has some probability mass.
  2. Think about your model.
    • Perhaps reconsider the constraints on your parameters.
    • Rethink priors. The prior on mu_p is pretty narrow. Should it be if you're really saying mu_p could be between 0 and 10?


That's it for now. Hopefully that's enough to get your model working.



Daniel
